Entourer de tous côtés quelque chose avec du papier, une étoffe, un linge, etc., qui couvre, qui environne de tous côtés.

examples.text: Un brouillard fumeux, ressemblant à celui de l’été indien, enveloppait toutes choses et ajoutait naturellement à mon incertitude.

glosses: To surround, enclose or enfold.

examples.text: In the fulness of time there was an eruption of the merry-makers to the sidewalk. The uninvited guests enveloped and permeated them, and upon the night air rose joyous cries, congratulations, laughter and unclassified noises born of McGary's oblations to the hymeneal scene.
(b) sporophyte with foot reduced, the entire sporophyte enveloped by the calyptra, which is ± stipitate at the base.

glosses: To encircle something or simultaneously extend in all directions.

examples.text: The hovel stood in the centre of what had once been a vegetable garden, but was now a patch of rank weeds. Surrounding this, almost like a zareba, was an irregular ring of gorse and brambles, an unclaimed vestige of the original common.

examples.text: The lions surrounded the deer herd so they had no way to escape.

glosses: Anything, such as a fence or border, that surrounds something.

examples.text:

examples.text: Christmas gifts are commonly known to be wrapped in paper.

examples.text: A snake wraps itself around its prey.
